title: The New York invitation and La Rocca forming a band
summary: Laine was asked to take a band to New York but while he played a parade La Rocca was approached and organized the band that went without him.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: But to tell you, even so, Buddy Bolton was my age and started out when I started out. That'd be a colored band. That wouldn't be the first white band ever organized a ragtime band. No, no.
We're talking about a ragtime band regardless of color. I'm not thinking about color. Just thinking about the style of music, you know.
Well, that's how it was. That fellas went to New York and all you know. Now, they wrote for me to go up there.

And I'll tell you, it was one night. How I come not to go up there, it was another political parade I was playing. And I had this man, La Rocca, in the band. Nick La Rocca? He played with me, too. I'd pick up La Rocca when he hardly heard anything about it, Trumper. And I'm playing the music on the street. Some fellas stepped in and was told to me after.
I'll ask Paul. I'll ask Paul.

I want to know who's the leader of the band. I want to get a band to go to New York. La Rocca, give them a note. And this fella goes to La Rocca's house. You see, La Rocca and La Rocca organize a band goes to New York. I see. Unnoticed to me.

Well, this was a long, long time after you first started music. Oh, yes. This was about 1915 or 16. Oh, a long time. A long time after, yeah. Well, let's see. You started playing when you were about 16 years old professionally for money. Yes. And that would have been about 1882, 1883, 1885, something like that. Something along that. About 1887. Well, now, Buddy Bolton did not start playing until about the 1890s, right?
